listenings.text: Things are moving, I would say. We sent some things last week, maybe. A few items are still open. We are waiting for some people. It should all be fine soon, I hope.

As per your email, here is where we are. The proposal was sent on Friday. The employee file has not been received yet, so it is still pending. The approval will be given on the twentieth. Nothing else is open on our side.

paras: As per our call this morning, here is what was agreed. The signed contract will be sent to you by Tuesday. The staff list needs to be sent to us by Thursday.
Two points are still open. The budget has not been approved yet, and London meets on the twentieth. The bank details have not been confirmed, so the first invoice will not be issued this month.
One thing worth saying: we completed the last transition of this size two days early. Please quote AUR-2418 in any reply.
reading.source: Composite follow-up email written for this lesson.

matching.title: The four words again
defs: exactly as agreed before, pointing back to something
waiting, not decided yet, still open
the formal yes that lets the work start
to say the message arrived, before you answer it

arguebank.label: Useful language
items: I would rather receive ... , because ...
There are no dates in ...
I know what I have to do.
I could answer it in thirty seconds.
It says who, what and when.
Polite is not the same as useful.
The passive keeps the blame out of it.
The active keeps the credit in it.
